description: behavioral-spec.md's 'Complete, closed audit' table (line 171) claims registry.json's LIVE `earn/clip-producer` slot has 'no' vulnerable env-clobbering pattern ('Not applicable — clean'). This is factually wrong: the slot's real entrypoint, skills/earn/clip-producer/run.sh:19, does `exec bash "$(...)/../clip"/producer.sh" "$@"` — `exec` replaces the process image in place (same PID, same inherited env, including whatever real per-instance ANICCA_HOME index.mjs's buildSkillEnv/spawn() set for this dispatch) — and skills/earn/clip/producer.sh:22 then runs the exact unfixed vulnerable preamble `set -a; . "$HOME/.openclaw/.env" 2>/dev/null; set +a` with no save/restore of the caller's ANICCA_HOME, inside that SAME live, per-instance-dispatched process. This is precisely the dispatch path (index.mjs -> a registry.json LIVE slot -> spawn() with a per-instance ANICCA_HOME) that REQ-004's own scope criterion defines as in-scope ('A file is in scope... if it is the literal entrypoint of a registry.json slot with status live... this dispatch path can ever hand a script the wrong instance's identity'), yet the audit did not trace the exec-chain past run.sh's own one-line body, so it missed that producer.sh's vulnerable preamble runs inside that same in-scope process. REQ-003 (behavioral-spec.md lines 89-107) already established the precedent that a DORMANT instance of this pattern in a live-dispatched code path must still be fixed ('it is a zero-risk, already-proven-safe change... with no proportionate reason to leave latent') — self/spawn-child and economy/lending were fixed on exactly that basis despite being dormant. producer.sh is dormant today only because nothing in skills/earn/clip/ currently reads ANICCA_HOME (confirmed: zero matches via grep across the whole directory) — but it is live-slot-reachable in a way the other 3 iteration-5-flagged files (clip-promote/run.sh — not a registry.json slot at all; x402-sell/serve-mainnet-boot.sh — standalone launchd daemon, and its slot `x402_sell`'s real dir is skills/earn not skills/earn/x402-sell; clip-producer.plist — standalone launchd daemon, no caller identity to clobber) genuinely are not. The 'closed, exhaustively checkable' claim in verification-architecture.md lines 91-98 ('Every one of them was checked directly against its declared dir/entrypoint') is therefore not true for this slot, and the reclassification of iteration-5's producer.sh finding as fully out-of-scope is not defensible for this one file.
requiredFix: Route skills/earn/clip/producer.sh's env-loading preamble (line 22) through skills/_shared/lib/load-instance-env.sh, identically to the 4 already-fixed call sites (this also automatically closes the same gap for producer.sh's two other callers, earn/clip-promote/run.sh and the clip-producer.plist standalone daemon, at zero extra cost). Then correct behavioral-spec.md's audit-table row for earn/clip-producer from 'no'/'clean' to 'FIXED', and add a note to REQ-004/REQ-003 that scope-checking a live slot's 'literal entrypoint' must trace exec-chains, not just the entrypoint file's own inline content.
